title: Search Results
body:
Search Results

When you search for an item, your buying options are categorized into different tabs in the search results.

Using the search bar, you can search for an item or service by keyword, supplier, or part number. When you enter a search term, suggested options display, as shown in the following figure.
Tip

If your site's default locale is set to an Asian language, you must enter at least two characters when you conduct searches throughout guided buying.

The tabs available and the links you can access are based on your site's configuration and your group membership. In the following figure, the Explore, Catalogs, Item hierarchy, Spot Buy catalog, Suppliers, Forms, and Explore more results tabs are available.

The following tabs display in the search results:

  • Explore: This tab displays the most popular search results from each tab.

  • Catalog: This tab displays results for items and services from your catalog. When you see the Buy from supplier option for an item, you must navigate to the supplier's site to add the item to your cart.

  • Item hierarchy: This tab displays results for service items containing hierarchical items, which allows users to create two-level service purchase requests. For example, if you need to request a catering service, the child line items could be the clearning service and the rental equipment.

  • Spot buy catalog: This tab displays results for items and services that aren't available through your catalog. You can use this option to request non-catalog items without having to specify a supplier. For more information on spot buy capability, see Spot Buy Capability in Guided Buying.

  • Suppliers: This tab displays the suppliers you can purchase from, results are listed as supplier tiles. When you open a supplier tile, you can find more information about the supplier and if available, find forms for items or services defaulted to that supplier. For more information, see Suppliers.

  • Forms: The tab displays custom forms your organization created for completing different procurement activities. For example, there could be forms for requesting items or services, creating a project, or transferring ownership of a document. Your organization may create forms for repeat purchases like, "Requesting a clearing service". For more information, see Forms.

  • Explore more results: The results on this tab are based on your organization's most recently used options: forms, links to external sites, or landing page tiles, for example.
